5	% Paradigm 1: Grammar-Constrained Decoding
6	% ===========================================================================
7	\paragraph{Grammar-Constrained Decoding.}
8	Recent work has established efficient algorithms for restricting LLM outputs to conform to context-free grammars, ensuring structural validity of generated text.
9	%
10	XGrammar~\cite{dong2025xgrammar} partitions the vocabulary into context-independent and context-dependent tokens, achieving 100$\times$ speedup over prior CFG-constrained decoding via persistent pushdown automata.
11	%
12	Outlines~\cite{willard2023outlines} reformulates constrained generation as finite-state machine transitions with offline vocabulary indexing, while LMQL~\cite{beurer-kellner2023lmql} introduces a declarative query language that compiles type, length, and regex constraints into token-level masks.
13	%
14	A parallel line addresses the \emph{distribution distortion} introduced by naive token masking: DOMINO~\cite{beurer-kellner2024domino} minimizes distributional divergence during CFG enforcement, and ASAp~\cite{park2024grammar} provides an unbiased sampling algorithm that preserves the original LM distribution under grammar constraints.
15	%
16	\textbf{Distinction:} OntoCoDec's grammar layer builds on XGrammar for structural (JSON schema + enum) constraints, but these methods operate exclusively at the syntactic level---they ensure format validity but cannot enforce cross-field semantic constraints such as ontology domain/range rules.
17	
18	% TODO: Expand with 2-3 sentences on how grammar-constrained decoding has become
19	% the de facto standard for structured output, and why the syntactic-only limitation
20	% motivates our semantic extension.
21	
22	% ===========================================================================
23	% Paradigm 1.5: Semantic Constrained Decoding for Code
24	% ===========================================================================
25	\paragraph{Semantic Constrained Decoding for Code.}
26	In programming-language generation, constrained decoding has been extended beyond syntax to enforce semantic properties such as type correctness.
27	%
28	Synchromesh~\cite{synchromesh_neurips2022} pioneers Constrained Semantic Decoding (CSD), which enforces syntax, type, and scope constraints simultaneously during code generation from pre-trained LMs, establishing that semantic constraints can be compiled into token-level filtering without fine-tuning.
29	%
30	MGD~\cite{mgd_neurips2023} uses static-analysis monitors to perform type checking at decode time, enabling SantaCoder-1.1B to outperform text-davinci-003 on repository-level code completion by enforcing type-correct identifier usage.
31	%
32	Most recently, \citet{pldi2025_type_constrained_codegen} compile full type systems into prefix automata for token-level logits masking, reducing compilation errors by over 50\%---the closest mechanistic analog to OntoCoDec, applying the same ``type system $\to$ automaton $\to$ logits mask'' pipeline.
33	%
34	\textbf{Distinction:} These methods demonstrate that semantic (type) constraints at decode time are both feasible and highly effective---but exclusively in the code domain, where type systems are formally specified. OntoCoDec is the first to migrate this paradigm to information extraction, compiling IE ontology axioms (domain/range constraints) into an analogous decoding-time enforcement mechanism.
35	
36	% TODO: Expand with 1-2 sentences on the technical differences between PL type
37	% systems and IE ontology axioms (e.g., subtyping vs. domain/range), and how
38	% OntoCoDec bridges this gap.
39	
40	% ===========================================================================
41	% Paradigm 2: Vocabulary/Type-Constrained Generation
42	% ===========================================================================
43	\paragraph{Vocabulary and Type-Constrained Generation.}
44	The idea of enforcing entity-type compatibility constraints for IE dates back to pre-neural methods: \citet{roth_yih_2004} formulate joint entity and relation identification as an integer linear program (ILP) that enforces type constraints---e.g., EMP-ORG only between PER and ORG entities---establishing the principle that relational type compatibility should be a hard constraint, not a soft preference.
45	%
46	In the autoregressive era, GENRE~\cite{decao2021genre} pioneers trie-based constrained beam search for autoregressive entity retrieval, limiting each decoding step to tokens consistent with valid entity names.
47	%
48	GenIE~\cite{josifoski2022genie} extends this to end-to-end IE with state-based constraints that enforce valid triple structures, though it requires task-specific fine-tuning.
49	%
50	AdaKGC~\cite{adakgc_emnlp2023} introduces schema-constrained dynamic decoding with trie-based prefix trees that adapt to the target schema, enforcing that generated entity and relation names belong to a predefined inventory---a vocabulary-level constraint that ensures name validity but not type compatibility.
51	%
52	GCD~\cite{geng2023gcd} provides a unified grammar-constrained decoding framework for structured NLP tasks including IE, introducing input-dependent grammars for greater flexibility.
53	%
54	NeuroLogic Decoding~\cite{lu2021neurologic} expresses lexical inclusion/exclusion constraints as predicate logic formulas enforced during beam search.
55	%
56	\textbf{Distinction:} These approaches constrain \emph{which tokens} can appear (vocabulary membership) but not \emph{which type combinations} are valid for a given relation. OntoCoDec's semantic layer enforces relational constraints---e.g., that the head entity of relation $R$ must belong to type set $\mathcal{D}(R)$---which cannot be expressed as static vocabulary restrictions. Roth \& Yih's ILP formulation shares the same type-compatibility motivation but operates as a post-hoc reranker over discrete candidates, whereas OntoCoDec integrates enforcement directly into autoregressive decoding.
57	
58	% TODO: Add 1-2 sentences positioning GCD as the closest precursor (same logits-masking
59	% mechanism for IE) and clarifying that OntoCoDec extends from syntactic to semantic constraints.
60	
61	% ===========================================================================
62	% Paradigm 3: Structural Constraints for IE
63	% ===========================================================================
64	\paragraph{Structural Constraints via Training and Prompting.}
65	An orthogonal approach encodes IE output structure through model training or prompt design rather than decoding-time enforcement.
66	%
67	UIE~\cite{lu2022uie} defines a Structured Extraction Language and trains a unified text-to-structure model across 13 IE datasets, relying on large-scale pre-training to produce schema-compliant outputs.
68	%
69	GoLLIE~\cite{sainz2024gollie} expresses annotation guidelines as Python dataclass definitions, fine-tuning Code-LLaMA to generate typed code, achieving strong zero-shot transfer to unseen IE schemas.
70	%
71	KnowCoder~\cite{knowcoder_acl2024} takes this further by encoding 29K entity types from Wikidata as a Python class hierarchy, training a Code-LLM to generate structured extraction code that implicitly respects type inheritance---the most comprehensive schema-as-code approach to date.
72	%
73	CodeIE~\cite{li2023codeie} reformulates IE as code generation, leveraging the implicit type structure of programming languages.
74	%
75	ADELIE~\cite{qi2024adelie} uses SFT and DPO to align LLMs on IE tasks, achieving SOTA among open-source models while preserving general capabilities.
76	%
77	EnriCo~\cite{zaratiana2024enrico} applies Answer Set Programming (ASP) constraints during decoding of joint entity-relation extraction models, enforcing structural type compatibility at generation time---a decoding-time approach, though with model-specific (non-ontology-driven) constraints.
78	%
79	\textbf{Distinction:} Training-based methods provide \emph{soft} structural guidance---the model learns to prefer valid outputs but offers no compliance guarantee at inference time. EnriCo's ASP constraints are hard but model-specific and require manual rule authoring. OntoCoDec provides \emph{hard} decoding-time enforcement that is training-free, automatically compiled from ontology schemas, and composable with any of these approaches.
80	
81	% TODO: Expand with discussion of how training-based and decoding-time approaches
82	% are complementary (e.g., GoLLIE + OntoCoDec), not competing.
83	
84	% ===========================================================================
85	% Paradigm 4: Type-Checking / Ontology Validation
86	% ===========================================================================
87	\paragraph{Post-hoc Ontology Validation.}
88	Rather than constraining generation, several methods validate LLM outputs against ontological rules after generation.
89	%
90	ODKE+~\cite{khorshidi2025odke} dynamically generates ontology snippets containing domain/range constraints as prompt context, achieving 98.8\% precision across 195 predicates at web scale---but constraint adherence relies on prompt-level guidance, not enforcement.
91	%
92	SPIRES/OntoGPT~\cite{spires_2024} provides an ontology-based extraction framework that grounds LLM outputs against OBO ontologies post-generation, representing the prompt-then-validate paradigm in the biomedical domain.
93	%
94	OntoLogX~\cite{ontologx_2025} applies SHACL validation to LLM-generated knowledge graphs, iteratively correcting constraint violations and reducing them by approximately 10$\times$---demonstrating the detect-then-fix paradigm's effectiveness but also its inherent multi-pass cost.
95	%
96	\citet{upadhyay2023openie} inject entity-type knowledge as constraints into Open IE via both constrained inference and constraint-aware training, improving F1 by 29\% on CaRB.
97	%
98	\citet{regino2025kgcurator} propose a multi-stage LLM pipeline for validating RDF triple insertions against domain/range constraints, representing the post-hoc validation paradigm.
99	%
100	\citet{ekaw2024_ontology_beam} introduce ontology-constrained beam scoring for clinical summarization, applying soft biases (not hard masks) during beam search to steer outputs toward ontology-compliant terms---a middle ground between unconstrained generation and hard enforcement.
101	%
102	\textbf{Distinction:} Post-hoc validation detects violations after generation, requiring rejection or correction cycles that waste compute (14--15\% of generated triples contain domain/range violations in our setting). OntoCoDec \emph{prevents} violations during decoding, redirecting probability mass to valid alternatives rather than discarding invalid outputs. Soft-constraint approaches like EKAW'24 reduce but cannot eliminate violations, whereas OntoCoDec provides hard guarantees.
103	
104	% TODO: Add quantitative comparison of compute cost: post-hoc rejection vs.
105	% preventive enforcement (marginal overhead of logits masking vs. wasted tokens).
106	
107	% ===========================================================================
108	% Paradigm 5: Constrained Decoding Quality Concerns
109	% ===========================================================================
110	\paragraph{Quality Impact of Constrained Decoding.}
111	A growing body of work raises concerns that constrained decoding degrades LLM generation quality, particularly for reasoning-intensive tasks.
112	%
113	\citet{tam2024letmespeak} show that rigid format constraints (JSON, XML) harm performance on math and multi-hop QA but benefit classification-style tasks such as slot filling.
114	%
115	CRANE~\cite{banerjee2025crane} provides theoretical analysis of why restricting outputs to narrow grammars suppresses chain-of-thought reasoning, proposing an alternating strategy between unconstrained reasoning and constrained output phases.
116	%
117	\citet{schall2025hiddencost} conduct a systematic study across 11 models, finding 10--30\% semantic correctness degradation on reasoning tasks under structural constraints.
118	%
119	\citet{zhou2026snowballing} identify ``structure snowballing''---a failure mode where format compliance cognitive load traps models in structural patterns rather than improving reasoning during self-correction.
120	%
121	\textbf{Distinction:} OntoCoDec addresses this concern empirically: on SciERC, domain/range violations decrease from 15.4\% to 0.93\% ($\downarrow$94\%) with \emph{zero} F1 degradation (R-F1 +0.13pp, not significant). IE is an extraction task where constrained decoding's impact is minimal~\cite{tam2024letmespeak}, and OntoCoDec's constraints target only type tokens, leaving free-text spans unconstrained.
122

124	% CRANE's alternating approach, and noting that IE's extraction nature
125	% inherently avoids the reasoning-degradation regime.
126

129	% ===========================================================================
130	\paragraph{Our Approach.}
131	OntoCoDec occupies a unique position in this landscape: it is the first system to automatically compile IE ontology schemas---including domain/range axioms---into decoding-time semantic constraints, extending grammar-constrained decoding from syntactic to semantic enforcement.
132	%
133	Unlike vocabulary-constrained methods that restrict individual tokens, OntoCoDec enforces \emph{cross-field relational constraints} through a stateful entity registry that tracks extracted types during autoregressive generation.
134	%
135	Unlike training-based IE systems, OntoCoDec is training-free and provides hard compliance guarantees; unlike post-hoc validation, it prevents violations rather than detecting them, redirecting probability mass to valid alternatives at zero quality cost.

%

%
Most recently, \citet{pldi2025_type_constrained_codegen} compile full type systems into prefix automata for token-level logits masking, reducing compilation errors by over 50\%---the closest mechanistic analog to OntoCoDec, applying the same ``type system $\to$ automaton $\to$ logits mask'' pipeline.
%
\textbf{Distinction:} These methods demonstrate that semantic (type) constraints at decode time are both feasible and highly effective---but exclusively in the code domain, where type systems are formally specified. OntoCoDec is the first to migrate this paradigm to information extraction, compiling IE ontology axioms (domain/range constraints) into an analogous decoding-time enforcement mechanism.

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 2: Vocabulary/Type-Constrained Generation
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Vocabulary and Type-Constrained Generation.}
The idea of enforcing entity-type compatibility constraints for IE dates back to pre-neural methods: \citet{roth_yih_2004} formulate joint entity and relation identification as an integer linear program (ILP) that enforces type constraints---e.g., EMP-ORG only between PER and ORG entities---establishing the principle that relational type compatibility should be a hard constraint, not a soft preference.
%
In the autoregressive era, GENRE~\cite{decao2021genre} pioneers trie-based constrained beam search for autoregressive entity retrieval, limiting each decoding step to tokens consistent with valid entity names.
%
GenIE~\cite{josifoski2022genie} extends this to end-to-end IE with state-based constraints that enforce valid triple structures, though it requires task-specific fine-tuning.
%
AdaKGC~\cite{adakgc_emnlp2023} introduces schema-constrained dynamic decoding with trie-based prefix trees that adapt to the target schema, enforcing that generated entity and relation names belong to a predefined inventory---a vocabulary-level constraint that ensures name validity but not type compatibility.
%
GCD~\cite{geng2023gcd} provides a unified grammar-constrained decoding framework for structured NLP tasks including IE, introducing input-dependent grammars for greater flexibility.
%
NeuroLogic Decoding~\cite{lu2021neurologic} expresses lexical inclusion/exclusion constraints as predicate logic formulas enforced during beam search.
%
\textbf{Distinction:} These approaches constrain \emph{which tokens} can appear (vocabulary membership) but not \emph{which type combinations} are valid for a given relation. OntoCoDec's semantic layer enforces relational constraints---e.g., that the head entity of relation $R$ must belong to type set $\mathcal{D}(R)$---which cannot be expressed as static vocabulary restrictions. Roth \& Yih's ILP formulation shares the same type-compatibility motivation but operates as a post-hoc reranker over discrete candidates, whereas OntoCoDec integrates enforcement directly into autoregressive decoding.

% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Structural Constraints via Training and Prompting.}
An orthogonal approach encodes IE output structure through model training or prompt design rather than decoding-time enforcement.
%
UIE~\cite{lu2022uie} defines a Structured Extraction Language and trains a unified text-to-structure model across 13 IE datasets, relying on large-scale pre-training to produce schema-compliant outputs.
%
GoLLIE~\cite{sainz2024gollie} expresses annotation guidelines as Python dataclass definitions, fine-tuning Code-LLaMA to generate typed code, achieving strong zero-shot transfer to unseen IE schemas.
%
KnowCoder~\cite{knowcoder_acl2024} takes this further by encoding 29K entity types from Wikidata as a Python class hierarchy, training a Code-LLM to generate structured extraction code that implicitly respects type inheritance---the most comprehensive schema-as-code approach to date.
%

%
ADELIE~\cite{qi2024adelie} uses SFT and DPO to align LLMs on IE tasks, achieving SOTA among open-source models while preserving general capabilities.
%
EnriCo~\cite{zaratiana2024enrico} applies Answer Set Programming (ASP) constraints during decoding of joint entity-relation extraction models, enforcing structural type compatibility at generation time---a decoding-time approach, though with model-specific (non-ontology-driven) constraints.
%
\textbf{Distinction:} Training-based methods provide \emph{soft} structural guidance---the model learns to prefer valid outputs but offers no compliance guarantee at inference time. EnriCo's ASP constraints are hard but model-specific and require manual rule authoring. OntoCoDec provides \emph{hard} decoding-time enforcement that is training-free, automatically compiled from ontology schemas, and composable with any of these approaches.

% ===========================================================================

% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Post-hoc Ontology Validation.}
Rather than constraining generation, several methods validate LLM outputs against ontological rules after generation.
%
ODKE+~\cite{khorshidi2025odke} dynamically generates ontology snippets containing domain/range constraints as prompt context, achieving 98.8\% precision across 195 predicates at web scale---but constraint adherence relies on prompt-level guidance, not enforcement.
%

%
OntoLogX~\cite{ontologx_2025} applies SHACL validation to LLM-generated knowledge graphs, iteratively correcting constraint violations and reducing them by approximately 10$\times$---demonstrating the detect-then-fix paradigm's effectiveness but also its inherent multi-pass cost.
%
\citet{upadhyay2023openie} inject entity-type knowledge as constraints into Open IE via both constrained inference and constraint-aware training, improving F1 by 29\% on CaRB.
%
\citet{regino2025kgcurator} propose a multi-stage LLM pipeline for validating RDF triple insertions against domain/range constraints, representing the post-hoc validation paradigm.
%
\citet{ekaw2024_ontology_beam} introduce ontology-constrained beam scoring for clinical summarization, applying soft biases (not hard masks) during beam search to steer outputs toward ontology-compliant terms---a middle ground between unconstrained generation and hard enforcement.
%
\textbf{Distinction:} Post-hoc validation detects violations after generation, requiring rejection or correction cycles that waste compute (14--15\% of generated triples contain domain/range violations in our setting). OntoCoDec \emph{prevents} violations during decoding, redirecting probability mass to valid alternatives rather than discarding invalid outputs. Soft-constraint approaches like EKAW'24 reduce but cannot eliminate violations, whereas OntoCoDec provides hard guarantees.

\paragraph{Quality Impact of Constrained Decoding.}
A growing body of work raises concerns that constrained decoding degrades LLM generation quality, particularly for reasoning-intensive tasks.

%

%
\citet{zhou2026snowballing} identify ``structure snowballing''---a failure mode where format compliance cognitive load traps models in structural patterns rather than improving reasoning during self-correction.
%

\paragraph{Our Approach.}
OntoCoDec occupies a unique position in this landscape: it is the first system to automatically compile IE ontology schemas---including domain/range axioms---into decoding-time semantic constraints, extending grammar-constrained decoding from syntactic to semantic enforcement.
%
Unlike vocabulary-constrained methods that restrict individual tokens, OntoCoDec enforces \emph{cross-field relational constraints} through a stateful entity registry that tracks extracted types during autoregressive generation.
%
Unlike training-based IE systems, OntoCoDec is training-free and provides hard compliance guarantees; unlike post-hoc validation, it prevents violations rather than detecting them, redirecting probability mass to valid alternatives at zero quality cost.

\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related_work}

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 1: Grammar-Constrained Decoding
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Grammar-Constrained Decoding.}
Recent work has established efficient algorithms for restricting LLM outputs to conform to context-free grammars, making grammar-constrained decoding the de facto standard for obtaining structured output from language models.
XGrammar~\cite{dong2025xgrammar} partitions the vocabulary into context-independent and context-dependent tokens and maintains persistent pushdown automata across decoding steps, achieving up to 100$\times$ speedup over prior CFG-constrained decoding methods.
Outlines~\cite{willard2023outlines} reformulates constrained generation as finite-state machine transitions with offline vocabulary indexing, enabling efficient enforcement of regular-expression and JSON-schema constraints without runtime overhead per token.
LMQL~\cite{beurer-kellner2023lmql} introduces a declarative query language that compiles type, length, and regex constraints into token-level masks, providing a programmable interface for specifying multi-variable output structures.
These systems ensure that every generated token belongs to a grammar-valid continuation, but they do not address the \emph{distribution distortion} introduced by naive token masking.
A parallel line of work tackles this problem directly: DOMINO~\cite{beurer-kellner2024domino} minimizes distributional divergence during CFG enforcement by formulating mask selection as an optimization problem, and ASAp~\cite{park2024grammar} provides a provably unbiased sampling algorithm that preserves the original LM distribution under grammar constraints.
Together, these advances have made grammar-constrained decoding both fast and statistically principled, establishing a robust foundation for structured generation.
However, all of these methods operate exclusively at the syntactic level---they ensure format validity (e.g., well-formed JSON, valid enum values) but cannot enforce cross-field semantic constraints such as ontology domain/range rules that depend on previously generated content.
This syntactic-only limitation motivates OntoCoDec's semantic extension: our grammar layer builds on XGrammar for structural (JSON schema and enum) constraints, while a second semantic layer enforces relational type constraints that are inherently beyond the expressive power of context-free grammars.

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 1.5: Semantic Constrained Decoding for Code
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Semantic Constrained Decoding for Code.}
In programming-language generation, constrained decoding has been extended beyond syntax to enforce semantic properties such as type correctness, demonstrating that richer-than-CFG constraints can be compiled into token-level filtering.
Synchromesh~\cite{synchromesh_neurips2022} pioneers Constrained Semantic Decoding (CSD), which enforces syntax, type, and scope constraints simultaneously during code generation from pre-trained LMs without fine-tuning, establishing that semantic constraints can be expressed as dynamic token masks conditioned on the generation prefix.
MGD~\cite{mgd_neurips2023} uses static-analysis monitors to perform incremental type checking at decode time, enabling SantaCoder-1.1B to outperform text-davinci-003 on repository-level code completion by ensuring that every generated identifier is type-correct with respect to the surrounding code context.
Most recently, \citet{pldi2025_type_constrained_codegen} compile full type systems---including generic types and subtyping---into prefix automata for token-level logits masking, reducing compilation errors by over 50\%.
This last system is the closest mechanistic analog to OntoCoDec, applying the same ``type system $\to$ automaton $\to$ logits mask'' pipeline, though in a fundamentally different domain.
The key technical difference lies in the constraint structure: programming-language type systems feature deep subtyping hierarchies and parametric polymorphism, whereas IE ontology axioms specify flat domain/range sets---a relation $R$ accepts head entities from set $\mathcal{D}(R)$ and tail entities from set $\mathcal{R}(R)$, with no subtype chains.
Conversely, IE introduces a challenge absent in code generation: the constraint target (entity type) must be inferred from free-text spans rather than read from declared type annotations, requiring a stateful entity registry that tracks extracted types during autoregressive generation.
These methods collectively demonstrate that semantic (type) constraints at decode time are both feasible and highly effective, but exclusively in the code domain where type systems are formally specified.
OntoCoDec is the first to migrate type-constrained decoding from code generation to information extraction, compiling IE ontology axioms (domain/range constraints) into an analogous decoding-time enforcement mechanism.

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 2: Vocabulary/Type-Constrained Generation
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Vocabulary and Type-Constrained Generation.}
The idea of enforcing entity-type compatibility constraints for information extraction dates back to pre-neural methods.
\citet{roth_yih_2004} formulate joint entity and relation identification as an integer linear program (ILP) that enforces type constraints---e.g., \textsc{Emp-Org} only between \textsc{Per} and \textsc{Org} entities---establishing the foundational principle that relational type compatibility should be a hard constraint, not a soft preference learned from data.
In the autoregressive era, GENRE~\cite{decao2021genre} pioneers trie-based constrained beam search for autoregressive entity retrieval, restricting each decoding step to tokens consistent with valid entity names from a predefined catalog.
GenIE~\cite{josifoski2022genie} extends this approach to end-to-end information extraction with state-based constraints that enforce valid triple structures, achieving strong performance on closed-world knowledge base population, though it requires task-specific fine-tuning on the target schema.
AdaKGC~\cite{adakgc_emnlp2023} introduces schema-constrained dynamic decoding with trie-based prefix trees that adapt to the target schema, enforcing that generated entity and relation names belong to a predefined inventory---a vocabulary-level constraint that ensures name validity but does not verify type compatibility between a relation and its arguments.
GCD~\cite{geng2023gcd} provides a unified grammar-constrained decoding framework for structured NLP tasks including IE, introducing input-dependent grammars that adapt constraints based on the source text---the closest precursor to OntoCoDec in applying logits masking to IE, though limited to syntactic constraints.
NeuroLogic Decoding~\cite{lu2021neurologic} expresses lexical inclusion and exclusion constraints as predicate logic formulas enforced during beam search, offering a general mechanism for token-level control that can encode vocabulary membership but not relational type rules.
These approaches constrain \emph{which tokens} can appear (vocabulary membership) but not \emph{which type combinations} are valid for a given relation.
OntoCoDec's semantic layer enforces relational constraints---e.g., that the head entity of relation $R$ must belong to type set $\mathcal{D}(R)$---which cannot be expressed as static vocabulary restrictions because the valid set depends on the relation type generated earlier in the same sequence.
While Roth \& Yih's ILP formulation shares the same type-compatibility motivation, it operates as a post-hoc reranker over discrete candidates; OntoCoDec integrates enforcement directly into autoregressive decoding, preventing violations rather than filtering them.

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 3: Structural Constraints for IE
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Structural Constraints via Training and Prompting.}
An orthogonal approach encodes IE output structure through model training or prompt design rather than decoding-time enforcement, relying on learned representations to produce schema-compliant outputs.
UIE~\cite{lu2022uie} defines a Structured Extraction Language and trains a unified text-to-structure model across 13 IE datasets, relying on large-scale pre-training to internalize output format constraints.
GoLLIE~\cite{sainz2024gollie} expresses annotation guidelines as Python dataclass definitions and fine-tunes Code-LLaMA to generate typed code, achieving strong zero-shot transfer to unseen IE schemas by leveraging the implicit type structure of programming languages.
KnowCoder~\cite{knowcoder_acl2024} takes this further by encoding 29K entity types from Wikidata as a Python class hierarchy, training a Code-LLM to generate structured extraction code that implicitly respects type inheritance---the most comprehensive schema-as-code approach to date.
CodeIE~\cite{li2023codeie} similarly reformulates IE as code generation, leveraging the structural regularity of programming languages to reduce output format errors.
ADELIE~\cite{qi2024adelie} uses SFT and DPO to align LLMs on IE tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results among open-source models while preserving general capabilities, though compliance with ontological constraints remains a learned soft preference rather than a guarantee.
EnriCo~\cite{zaratiana2024enrico} applies Answer Set Programming (ASP) constraints during decoding of joint entity-relation extraction models, enforcing structural type compatibility at generation time---a decoding-time approach, though with model-specific, manually authored constraints rather than ontology-driven compilation.
Training-based methods provide \emph{soft} structural guidance---the model learns to prefer valid outputs but cannot guarantee compliance at inference time, as demonstrated by non-trivial violation rates even in fine-tuned systems.
Importantly, training-based and decoding-time approaches are complementary rather than competing: a system like GoLLIE could be combined with OntoCoDec's constraint layers, using fine-tuning to maximize the probability of valid outputs while decoding-time enforcement eliminates residual violations.
OntoCoDec provides \emph{hard} decoding-time enforcement that is training-free, automatically compiled from ontology schemas, and composable with any of these training-based approaches.

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 4: Type-Checking / Ontology Validation
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Post-hoc Ontology Validation.}
Rather than constraining generation, several methods validate LLM outputs against ontological rules after generation, applying a detect-then-fix paradigm.
ODKE+~\cite{khorshidi2025odke} dynamically generates ontology snippets containing domain/range constraints as prompt context, achieving 98.8\% precision across 195 predicates at web scale---but constraint adherence relies on prompt-level guidance, not enforcement, leaving residual violations unaddressed.
SPIRES/OntoGPT~\cite{spires_2024} provides an ontology-based extraction framework that grounds LLM outputs against OBO ontologies post-generation, validating extracted entities and relations through ontology lookup and correcting mismatches in a second pass---representing the prompt-then-validate paradigm in the biomedical domain.
OntoLogX~\cite{ontologx_2025} applies SHACL validation to LLM-generated knowledge graphs, iteratively re-prompting the LLM to correct constraint violations and reducing them by approximately 10$\times$ across multiple correction rounds---demonstrating the detect-then-fix paradigm's effectiveness but also its inherent multi-pass cost.
\citet{upadhyay2023openie} inject entity-type knowledge as constraints into Open IE via both constrained inference and constraint-aware training, improving F1 by 29\% on CaRB, though their constrained inference operates over a discrete candidate set rather than during autoregressive generation.
\citet{regino2025kgcurator} propose a multi-stage LLM pipeline for validating RDF triple insertions against RDFS domain/range constraints, where each validation step requires a separate LLM call---effective but computationally expensive at scale.
\citet{ekaw2024_ontology_beam} introduce ontology-constrained beam scoring for clinical summarization, applying soft biases (not hard masks) during beam search to steer outputs toward ontology-compliant terms---a middle ground between unconstrained generation and hard enforcement that reduces but cannot eliminate violations.
Post-hoc validation detects violations after generation, requiring rejection or correction cycles that waste compute---in our setting, 15.37\% of generated triples contain domain/range violations under unconstrained decoding, representing substantial wasted generation effort.
OntoCoDec \emph{prevents} violations during decoding, redirecting probability mass to valid alternatives rather than discarding invalid outputs, with only marginal overhead from logits masking compared to the cost of regenerating or correcting violated triples.
Soft-constraint approaches such as ontology-weighted beam scoring reduce violation frequency but cannot eliminate it, whereas OntoCoDec achieves near-complete elimination (domain/range violations $\downarrow$94\%, from 15.37\% to 0.93\%).

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 5: Constrained Decoding Quality Concerns
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Quality Impact of Constrained Decoding.}
A growing body of work raises concerns that constrained decoding degrades LLM generation quality, particularly for reasoning-intensive tasks where format enforcement interferes with chain-of-thought processes.
\citet{tam2024letmespeak} conduct a comprehensive evaluation showing that rigid format constraints (JSON, XML) harm performance on math and multi-hop QA benchmarks but \emph{benefit} classification-style tasks such as slot filling---a distinction directly relevant to IE, which is fundamentally an extraction (classification-like) task rather than a reasoning task.
CRANE~\cite{banerjee2025crane} provides theoretical analysis of why restricting outputs to narrow grammars suppresses chain-of-thought reasoning by eliminating intermediate reasoning tokens, and proposes an alternating strategy between unconstrained reasoning phases and constrained output phases to mitigate this effect.
\citet{schall2025hiddencost} conduct a systematic study across 11 models and multiple benchmarks, finding 10--30\% semantic correctness degradation on reasoning tasks under structural constraints, with larger models showing greater absolute degradation.
\citet{zhou2026snowballing} identify ``structure snowballing''---a failure mode where format compliance cognitive load traps models in repetitive structural patterns rather than improving reasoning during self-correction iterations. % PENDING AUDIT: zhou2026snowballing may need replacement
These findings establish a legitimate concern for constrained decoding in reasoning-heavy applications.
However, information extraction occupies a fundamentally different regime: the model extracts entities and relations from input text rather than generating novel reasoning chains, and \citet{tam2024letmespeak}'s own results show that extraction-style tasks are robust to---or even benefit from---format constraints.
OntoCoDec addresses this concern empirically: on SciERC, domain/range violations decrease from 15.37\% to 0.93\% ($\downarrow$94\%) with \emph{zero} F1 degradation (R-F1 8.36\% vs.\ 8.23\% unconstrained, $+$0.13pp, not statistically significant).
Critically, OntoCoDec's constraints target only type tokens (entity types, relation labels), leaving free-text spans---entity surface forms and their boundaries---entirely unconstrained, which minimizes the distribution distortion that causes quality degradation in reasoning tasks.
OntoCoDec's S2 (two-pass) strategy can also be viewed as an instantiation of CRANE's alternating approach: the first pass performs unconstrained entity extraction, and the second pass applies relation-specific constraints compiled from the first pass's output, separating the extraction and constraint-enforcement phases.

% ===========================================================================
% Our Approach
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Our Approach.}
OntoCoDec occupies a unique position in this landscape: it is the first system to automatically compile IE ontology schemas---including domain/range axioms---into decoding-time semantic constraints, extending grammar-constrained decoding from syntactic to semantic enforcement.
Unlike vocabulary-constrained methods that restrict individual tokens to a fixed set, OntoCoDec enforces \emph{cross-field relational constraints} through a stateful entity registry that tracks extracted types during autoregressive generation, enabling dynamic constraint evaluation that depends on previously decoded content.
Unlike training-based IE systems, OntoCoDec is training-free and provides hard compliance guarantees at inference time; unlike post-hoc validation, it prevents violations rather than detecting them, redirecting probability mass to valid alternatives at near-complete elimination rates (domain/range violations 15.37\%$\to$0.93\%) and zero quality cost (R-F1 8.36\% vs.\ 8.23\% unconstrained).
The two constraint layers---grammar (structural) and semantic (relational)---compose via bitwise AND with an enabling dependency: the grammar layer ensures every generated type token belongs to the valid vocabulary, which enables the semantic layer to look up and enforce domain/range rules for that type.

OntoCoDec's semantic layer enforces relational constraints---e.g., that the head entity of relation $R$ must belong to type set $\mathcal{D}(R)$---which cannot be expressed as static vocabulary restrictions because the valid set depends on the relation type generated earlier in the same sequence.
While Roth \& Yih's ILP formulation shares the same type-compatibility motivation, it operates as a post-hoc reranker over discrete candidates; OntoCoDec integrates enforcement directly into autoregressive decoding, preventing violations rather than filtering them.

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 3: Structural Constraints for IE
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Structural Constraints via Training and Prompting.}
An orthogonal approach encodes IE output structure through model training or prompt design rather than decoding-time enforcement, relying on learned representations to produce schema-compliant outputs.
UIE~\cite{lu2022uie} defines a Structured Extraction Language and trains a unified text-to-structure model across 13 IE datasets, relying on large-scale pre-training to internalize output format constraints.
GoLLIE~\cite{sainz2024gollie} expresses annotation guidelines as Python dataclass definitions and fine-tunes Code-LLaMA to generate typed code, achieving strong zero-shot transfer to unseen IE schemas by leveraging the implicit type structure of programming languages.
KnowCoder~\cite{knowcoder_acl2024} takes this further by encoding 29K entity types from Wikidata as a Python class hierarchy, training a Code-LLM to generate structured extraction code that implicitly respects type inheritance---the most comprehensive schema-as-code approach to date.
CodeIE~\cite{li2023codeie} similarly reformulates IE as code generation, leveraging the structural regularity of programming languages to reduce output format errors.
ADELIE~\cite{qi2024adelie} uses SFT and DPO to align LLMs on IE tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results among open-source models while preserving general capabilities, though compliance with ontological constraints remains a learned soft preference rather than a guarantee.
EnriCo~\cite{zaratiana2024enrico} applies Answer Set Programming (ASP) constraints during decoding of joint entity-relation extraction models, enforcing structural type compatibility at generation time---a decoding-time approach, though with model-specific, manually authored constraints rather than ontology-driven compilation.
Training-based methods provide \emph{soft} structural guidance---the model learns to prefer valid outputs but cannot guarantee compliance at inference time, as demonstrated by non-trivial violation rates even in fine-tuned systems.
Importantly, training-based and decoding-time approaches are complementary rather than competing: a system like GoLLIE could be combined with OntoCoDec's constraint layers, using fine-tuning to maximize the probability of valid outputs while decoding-time enforcement eliminates residual violations.
OntoCoDec provides \emph{hard} decoding-time enforcement that is training-free, automatically compiled from ontology schemas, and composable with any of these training-based approaches.

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 4: Type-Checking / Ontology Validation
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Post-hoc Ontology Validation.}
Rather than constraining generation, several methods validate LLM outputs against ontological rules after generation, applying a detect-then-fix paradigm.
ODKE+~\cite{khorshidi2025odke} dynamically generates ontology snippets containing domain/range constraints as prompt context, achieving 98.8\% precision across 195 predicates at web scale---but constraint adherence relies on prompt-level guidance, not enforcement, leaving residual violations unaddressed.
SPIRES/OntoGPT~\cite{spires_2024} provides an ontology-based extraction framework that grounds LLM outputs against OBO ontologies post-generation, validating extracted entities and relations through ontology lookup and correcting mismatches in a second pass---representing the prompt-then-validate paradigm in the biomedical domain.
OntoLogX~\cite{ontologx_2025} applies SHACL validation to LLM-generated knowledge graphs, iteratively re-prompting the LLM to correct constraint violations and reducing them by approximately 10$\times$ across multiple correction rounds---demonstrating the detect-then-fix paradigm's effectiveness but also its inherent multi-pass cost.
\citet{upadhyay2023openie} inject entity-type knowledge as constraints into Open IE via both constrained inference and constraint-aware training, improving F1 by 29\% on CaRB, though their constrained inference operates over a discrete candidate set rather than during autoregressive generation.
\citet{regino2025kgcurator} propose a multi-stage LLM pipeline for validating RDF triple insertions against RDFS domain/range constraints, where each validation step requires a separate LLM call---effective but computationally expensive at scale.
\citet{ekaw2024_ontology_beam} introduce ontology-constrained beam scoring for clinical summarization, applying soft biases (not hard masks) during beam search to steer outputs toward ontology-compliant terms---a middle ground between unconstrained generation and hard enforcement that reduces but cannot eliminate violations.
Post-hoc validation detects violations after generation, requiring rejection or correction cycles that waste compute---in our setting, 15.37\% of generated triples contain domain/range violations under unconstrained decoding, representing substantial wasted generation effort.
OntoCoDec \emph{prevents} violations during decoding, redirecting probability mass to valid alternatives rather than discarding invalid outputs, with only marginal overhead from logits masking compared to the cost of regenerating or correcting violated triples.
Soft-constraint approaches such as ontology-weighted beam scoring reduce violation frequency but cannot eliminate it, whereas OntoCoDec achieves near-complete elimination (domain/range violations $\downarrow$94\%, from 15.37\% to 0.93\%).

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 5: Constrained Decoding Quality Concerns
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Quality Impact of Constrained Decoding.}
A growing body of work raises concerns that constrained decoding degrades LLM generation quality, particularly for reasoning-intensive tasks where format enforcement interferes with chain-of-thought processes.
\citet{tam2024letmespeak} conduct a comprehensive evaluation showing that rigid format constraints (JSON, XML) harm performance on math and multi-hop QA benchmarks but \emph{benefit} classification-style tasks such as slot filling---a distinction directly relevant to IE, which is fundamentally an extraction (classification-like) task rather than a reasoning task.
CRANE~\cite{banerjee2025crane} provides theoretical analysis of why restricting outputs to narrow grammars suppresses chain-of-thought reasoning by eliminating intermediate reasoning tokens, and proposes an alternating strategy between unconstrained reasoning phases and constrained output phases to mitigate this effect.
\citet{schall2025hiddencost} conduct a systematic study across 11 models and multiple benchmarks, finding 10--30\% semantic correctness degradation on reasoning tasks under structural constraints, with larger models showing greater absolute degradation.
\citet{zhou2026snowballing} identify ``structure snowballing''---a failure mode where format compliance cognitive load traps models in repetitive structural patterns rather than improving reasoning during self-correction iterations. % PENDING AUDIT: zhou2026snowballing may need replacement
These findings establish a legitimate concern for constrained decoding in reasoning-heavy applications.
However, information extraction occupies a fundamentally different regime: the model extracts entities and relations from input text rather than generating novel reasoning chains, and \citet{tam2024letmespeak}'s own results show that extraction-style tasks are robust to---or even benefit from---format constraints.
OntoCoDec addresses this concern empirically: on SciERC, domain/range violations decrease from 15.37\% to 0.93\% ($\downarrow$94\%) with \emph{zero} F1 degradation (R-F1 8.36\% vs.\ 8.23\% unconstrained, $+$0.13pp, not statistically significant).
Critically, OntoCoDec's constraints target only type tokens (entity types, relation labels), leaving free-text spans---entity surface forms and their boundaries---entirely unconstrained, which minimizes the distribution distortion that causes quality degradation in reasoning tasks.
OntoCoDec's S2 (two-pass) strategy can also be viewed as an instantiation of CRANE's alternating approach: the first pass performs unconstrained entity extraction, and the second pass applies relation-specific constraints compiled from the first pass's output, separating the extraction and constraint-enforcement phases.

% ===========================================================================
% Our Approach
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Our Approach.}
OntoCoDec occupies a unique position in this landscape: it is the first system to automatically compile IE ontology schemas---including domain/range axioms---into decoding-time semantic constraints, extending grammar-constrained decoding from syntactic to semantic enforcement.
Unlike vocabulary-constrained methods that restrict individual tokens to a fixed set, OntoCoDec enforces \emph{cross-field relational constraints} through a stateful entity registry that tracks extracted types during autoregressive generation, enabling dynamic constraint evaluation that depends on previously decoded content.
Unlike training-based IE systems, OntoCoDec is training-free and provides hard compliance guarantees at inference time; unlike post-hoc validation, it prevents violations rather than detecting them, redirecting probability mass to valid alternatives at near-complete elimination rates (domain/range violations 15.37\%$\to$0.93\%) and zero quality cost (R-F1 8.36\% vs.\ 8.23\% unconstrained).
The two constraint layers---grammar (structural) and semantic (relational)---compose via bitwise AND with an enabling dependency: the grammar layer ensures every generated type token belongs to the valid vocabulary, which enables the semantic layer to look up and enforce domain/range rules for that type.
